title: The Last Machine Again
premise: Odile Pemberton, navigator of the freighter Long Quiet, has spent eleven years running cargo between worlds that severed contact after the Meridian War, haunted by the memory-backups of her dead crew sleeping in the hold. When she intercepts a distress call in Old Vessic — a language extinct since the war's first atrocity — she recognizes it as the tongue of her own buried past and of the backups themselves. Pursued by a naval remnant that wants the message destroyed, Odile must choose between the found family aboard her ship and the duty she fled: delivering a peace accord that could end the war, or ignite its final act before the jump window closes. She delivers it, waking the backups as living witnesses, and the war ends not with surrender but with shared memory.
about_author: Jude Pemberton is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio officer who now writes from a converted lighthouse on the northern coast. Their fiction explores how people carry the dead forward without being crushed by the weight.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine jump run; she visits the cryo-hold where forty-one memory-backups sleep, including her own first death. Establishes her guilt and ritual of talking to them. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Cargo for Silent Ports
chapters.summary: Engineer Toma's POV. The crew unloads at a port that refuses to acknowledge them. Toma patches a failing coil and jokes to keep fear down. Beat: found family holding together through small kindnesses.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, flashback structure. How the Long Quiet's crew went dark after the Meridian War's broadcast massacres. Beat: the cost of survival by silence.

chapters.title: The Signal in Old Vessic
chapters.summary: Comms officer Sefa's POV. A repeating distress pattern arrives in a language officially extinct. Sefa secretly records it before reporting. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Backups Know
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She plays the signal near the hold; one backup, Rell, shows neural response. The dead may be able to translate. Beat: hope she doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Crew Vote
chapters.summary: Captain Ivo's POV. The crew debates answering the distress call against protocol. Ivo, who lost sons in the war, votes yes. Beat: duty versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Course to Kessel Drift
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Navigation sequence toward the signal source through contested space. Her hands remember routes her mind forbids. Beat: the body keeps old loyalties.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Amaranth
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They find the derelict broadcaster: a hospital ship scuttled in the war's opening atrocity. Beat: grief made physical.

chapters.title: Rell Wakes
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. Against regulations they partially wake backup Rell, who speaks Old Vessic and remembers the massacre firsthand. Beat: the past opens its eyes.

chapters.title: The Message in the Hull
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. The distress call is half of a negotiated armistice, recorded by dying medics; the other half lies in a naval vault. Beat: a message that is also an accusation.

chapters.title: Shadow on the Scope
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A navy corvette, the Vigilant, begins trailing them. Beat: invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Hail and Denial
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Tense comms exchange; Odile lies beautifully about their registry. Beat: love of the crew sharpening into deception.

chapters.title: What Odile Buried
chapters.summary: Odile's POV flashback. She was a war-time signals officer who translated the order that doomed the Amaranth. Beat: shame revealed, sympathy deepened.

chapters.title: The Vault at Corvane Station
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. Plan forms: infiltrate a decommissioned naval archive to retrieve the armistice's second half. Beat: resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Port of Strangers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Resupply stop where refugees from the war still live in camps; a child asks Rell if the killing stopped. Beat: stakes become human faces.

chapters.title: Vigilant Closes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The corvette demands boarding. First evasion maneuver through debris fields. Beat: adrenaline and guilt intertwined.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Navy officers come aboard under pretext; one recognizes Odile's voiceprint. Beat: terror of being known.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Remembered Her
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Casimir's POV. He served under Odile once; he lets them go but logs a partial report, torn between duty and doubt. Beat: the enemy gains a conscience.

chapters.title: Jump Window Mathematics
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The only corridor to the neutral mediation world closes in nineteen days. Everything must converge on that window. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Rell Deteriorates
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. The partial wake destabilizes; Rell's memories bleed into ship systems, broadcasting fragments. Beat: intimacy with the dead has a price.

chapters.title: Corvane Infiltration
chapters.summary: Ivo and Sefa's alternating POV. The vault break-in succeeds until an alarm trips. Beat: triumph turning to flight.

chapters.title: The Second Half
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reading the recovered accord: mutual amnesty contingent on public delivery by a named signatory — Odile herself. Beat: duty she cannot refuse.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Heart
chapters.summary: Crew meeting, multiple POVs. Some want to burn the message and stay hidden forever. Odile offers to leave alone. Beat: found family tested by love against safety.

chapters.title: Casimir's Choice
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Ordered to intercept and destroy the freighter, he requests verification instead and is confined. Beat: duty cracking from inside.

chapters.title: The Vigilant Mutinies
chapters.summary: Ensign Brava's POV. Half the corvette's crew refuses the destroy order; civil strife erupts aboard. Beat: the war's logic failing its own soldiers.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Shoals
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Full-tilt pursuit toward the jump window, both ships damaged. Beat: desperation and exhilaration.

chapters.title: Waking the Forty-One
chapters.summary: Toma and Rell's POV. To survive translation load, all backups are fully woken — the dead return as witnesses. Beat: resurrection as courage, not horror.

chapters.title: Testimony in Transit
chapters.summary: Rell and the awakened crew's POV. The dead record their testimony for the mediation council while the ship burns fuel it can't spare. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Beacon
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A resupply contact sells their position to the loyalist fleet. Beat: trust wounded, family rallying.

chapters.title: Ivo's Stand
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He takes a shuttle to draw off pursuers, buying hours. Beat: sacrifice offered, refused, then accepted.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Arrival at the jump threshold with minutes to spare and the loyalist vanguard behind. Beat: breath held.

chapters.title: Fire Across the Threshold
chapters.summary: Action climax, multiple POVs. The loyalists attack as the Long Quiet jumps; Ivo's shuttle is lost covering them. Beat: cost paid in full.

chapters.title: The Mediation Floor
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Before the assembled factions, she delivers the accord and confesses her role in the Amaranth. Beat: confession as the price of peace.

chapters.title: The Dead Speak
chapters.summary: Rell and the forty-one's POV. Testimony broadcasts simultaneously to every fleet; weapons stand down mid-order. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Casimir's Testimony
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. He confirms the cover-up from the navy's side, sealing the amnesty. Beat: reconciliation across lines.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence Broken
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. Fleets stand down; ports reopen; the crew walks a station where people say their names aloud. Beat: tenderness after terror.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Debate over whether the backups should sleep again or live. They choose life, imperfect and awake. Beat: choosing presence over haunting.

chapters.title: Letters to Ivo
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The crew writes to families of the lost, including Ivo's sons, carrying his last words home. Beat: mourning shared becomes mourning halved.

chapters.title: The Long Route Again
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Long Quiet takes a new charter: ferrying witnesses and messages between reconciled worlds. Beat: purpose renewed.

chapters.title: First Light on Open Water
chapters.summary: Odile's closing POV. At the hold's open door, no one sleeps there now; she still talks to the empty bunks, but out loud, unashamed. Final beat: memory carried as love, not burden.
